_comment: Hand-authored from SPEC.md before the v5 implementation existed. Each case gives per-task (pass_rate-producing) rollout outcomes and the verdict derived by reading the spec and doing the arithmetic by hand. Soft-axis numbers are held identical between arms unless a case says otherwise, so the pass clause is what is under test. Never regenerate from code.

cases.name: null_identical_harness
cases.why: The real regression case: one task flips by a single rollout, every soft axis is flat. Aggregate 2.75 -> 3.00 is +9.1 percent relative, under the 0.15 effect; the biggest per-task delta is 0.25, under 0.5. Neither disjunct fires.

cases.name: real_fix_half_the_rollouts
cases.why: A mutation that takes a failing task from 0/4 to 2/4. Per-task delta 0.5 meets material_task_delta exactly, and the rule is >=, so it fires.

cases.name: real_fix_one_rollout_only
cases.why: The acknowledged limitation. 0/4 to 1/4 is delta 0.25 per task and +6.25 percent aggregate (4.00 -> 4.25). Neither disjunct fires, so it does not promote on the pass axis. Recorded so the cost of the rule is visible in the fixtures, not just in prose.

cases.name: broad_small_gains_clear_the_aggregate_bar
cases.why: Three tasks each rise by one rollout from a low base: 1.00 -> 1.75 is +75 percent relative, clearing 0.15, while no single per-task delta reaches 0.5. The aggregate disjunct is what keeps this promotable.

cases.name: regression_still_hard_rejects
cases.why: Rule 3 is untouched by v5: a per-task held_in drop rejects regardless of how material any gain elsewhere is.

cases.name: held_out_floor_still_hard_rejects
cases.why: Rule 2 is untouched: a held_out drop rejects even with a material held_in gain.

cases.name: soft_axis_still_promotes_alone
cases.why: A candidate with no pass change at all still promotes on a soft-axis improvement past the effect threshold. v5 changes only the pass branch.
